why: Starts with familiar quality work and reviewable output. Existing requirements let QA assess value before connecting tools or running tests.
prerequisites: Required: agreed requirements, acceptance criteria and a test case template. A person can provide these artifacts.
milestone: Review cases for one feature. Confirm each case has valid requirement links, reproducible steps and a checkable expected result.

why: Builds on a test inventory to expose coverage gaps and duplicate scenarios. The comparison can be checked against a small known reference set.
prerequisites: Required: identified requirements, test cases and coverage rules. Cases may be written manually or produced in step 1.
milestone: Use a reference set with a known uncovered requirement and duplicate case. Confirm both are identified without treating a weak link as coverage.

why: Provides a useful quality deliverable immediately from existing or manual execution records. It needs no automated execution skill.
prerequisites: Required: completed test-cycle scope, execution records, defects and build identity. Existing or manual records satisfy this prerequisite.
milestone: Reconcile one test summary with its source cycle. Match all result counts, defects, scope exclusions and evidence references.

why: Extends the verified reporting approach to an active test cycle, making blockers and unexecuted work visible to the quality leader.
prerequisites: Required: planned test scope, current execution and defect records, reporting cutoff and agreed status definitions.
milestone: Compare a progress report with one source snapshot. Confirm blocked and unexecuted tests remain distinct and every total reconciles.

why: Uses the same quality evidence to improve reproducibility and classification. Human triage decisions make suggestions easy to evaluate.
prerequisites: Required: failure evidence, build/environment details, defect taxonomy and an existing defect register.
milestone: Review several defect drafts, including a duplicate. Confirm reproduction details and evidence, then have a triage owner assess suggested priority.

why: Combines coverage, results and defects once their reporting is understood. It supports a human test exit decision using explicit criteria.
prerequisites: Required: agreed exit criteria, current coverage/results, open defects and exception evidence. A named test owner makes the decision.
milestone: Assess one cycle with a deliberately unmet exit criterion. Confirm the gap is visible and the recommendation does not claim human approval.

why: Addresses ambiguities uncovered during the QA pilot. Precise criteria improve test design and give later skills observable success conditions.
prerequisites: Required: agreed requirement intent, business rules, examples and quality targets. Stakeholders resolve unclear behavior.
milestone: Review criteria for one feature with product and test owners. Confirm positive, negative and boundary behavior is observable.

why: Improves the quality and priority of the existing backlog before investing in broader discovery or delivery automation.
prerequisites: Required: draft requirements, scope, prioritization criteria, known dependencies and stakeholder value judgments.
milestone: Use a backlog sample containing ambiguity and conflicting requirements. Confirm both are flagged and each proposed priority has a rationale.

why: Introduces a repeatable review package once requirement quality checks are available. Agreement remains with the stakeholders.
prerequisites: Required: requirements, acceptance criteria, reviewer feedback, review checklist and decision owners.
milestone: Review one requirements baseline. Trace every finding and pending decision, and confirm unsigned items remain pending.

why: Adds stakeholder discovery after establishing how to judge requirement quality. The pilot can use existing interview notes.
prerequisites: Required: stakeholder notes or access to interviews, process evidence, problem context and known constraints.
milestone: Compare a needs register with one interview transcript. Confirm needs have source references and assumptions are separated from stated facts.

why: Expands the pilot into business boundaries after stakeholder needs can be reviewed. Existing scope can support every earlier step.
prerequisites: Required: stakeholder needs, business goals, constraints and product boundaries. A business owner agrees the resulting scope.
milestone: Review one scope proposal with a business owner. Confirm exclusions, measurable goals and unresolved assumptions are explicit.

why: Consolidates known requirements and quality risks into the plan that will govern environment preparation and test execution.
prerequisites: Required: requirements, architecture context, risks, milestones, available resources and applicable test policies.
milestone: Review a plan for one release. Confirm risks map to test levels and that entry, exit, suspension and resumption conditions are usable.

why: Turns scope into manageable work before estimating or scheduling it. Both implementation and test tasks should be visible.
prerequisites: Required: prioritized scope, acceptance criteria, reviewed design context and team backlog conventions.
milestone: Walk one feature from requirement to tasks. Confirm testing, dependencies and completion conditions are included without duplicate work.

why: Exposes sequencing constraints before estimates become a delivery commitment, including external teams and environment availability.
prerequisites: Required: task breakdown, component relationships, external commitments and environment or approval prerequisites.
milestone: Review one dependency map with delivery owners. Confirm known blockers, ownership and needed dates match source commitments.

why: Uses a task breakdown and known dependencies to produce estimates the team can challenge and compare with actual capacity.
prerequisites: Required: scoped tasks, historical data or expert estimates, team skills, availability and working calendar.
milestone: Estimate a small backlog with the team. Check range assumptions and capacity arithmetic, then compare estimates with a completed reference item.

why: Follows validated work, dependency and capacity inputs so the proposed schedule can be checked for feasibility.
prerequisites: Required: prioritized work, effort estimates, capacity, dependency commitments and milestone targets.
milestone: Review one iteration plan. Confirm planned load fits capacity and every scheduled item has its prerequisites available in time.

why: Establishes the environment and representative data required before automated tests can produce trustworthy evidence.
prerequisites: Required: test data needs, environment design, access authorization, configuration baseline and data handling rules.
milestone: Set up an isolated pilot environment. Verify configuration and synthetic or masked data, then repeat setup and cleanup successfully.

why: Creates runnable checks only after test cases and resources are usable. Existing runnable suites can satisfy later prerequisites instead.
prerequisites: Required: reviewed cases, stable interfaces, chosen framework, representative data and a ready test environment.
milestone: Automate a small stable case set. Demonstrate an expected pass and a deliberately introduced failure with useful evidence and repeatable cleanup.

why: Starts execution with a small critical-path suite in a test environment. The production variant waits for explicit live-service authorization.
prerequisites: Required: ready environment and data, runnable smoke suite, known deployed build and approved execution scope.
milestone: Run the pilot suite on a healthy test build and one with a broken critical path. Confirm the result changes and evidence identifies the failure.

why: Adds interface and data-exchange coverage after basic environment health is verifiable. Existing deployed systems can provide the build.
prerequisites: Required: ready integration environment/data, runnable integration tests, interface contracts and accessible dependencies or agreed stubs.
milestone: Validate one interface's normal exchange and an error response. Check contract assertions, correlation details and failure evidence.

why: Broadens execution to business behavior once the environment and interfaces can be checked reliably.
prerequisites: Required: ready test environment/data, runnable functional checks, test accounts and agreed acceptance criteria.
milestone: Execute one complete user journey plus a negative case. Confirm actual results and captured evidence support each expected outcome.

why: Reuses established checks to protect existing behavior, then evaluates targeted selection for defect fixes against known impacts.
prerequisites: Required: ready environment/data, runnable regression suite, coverage map, change impact analysis and target build.
milestone: Run a baseline suite, then select tests for a known change. Confirm an affected failure is detected and excluded coverage is documented.

why: Comes after repeatable functional execution because performance, security and other quality checks need specialized setup and explicit targets.
prerequisites: Required: approved scope/window, ready representative environment/data, runnable quality checks, agreed targets and monitoring tools.
milestone: Pilot one relevant quality attribute with its specialist. Reproduce a measurement and show how a controlled threshold breach is reported.

why: Uses reliable execution and defect records to verify fixes. A corrected build may be supplied manually by developers.
prerequisites: Required: corrected deployed build, ready environment/data, reproducible retest procedure or runnable check, and original defect evidence.
milestone: Retest a known fixed defect and an unfixed comparison. Confirm closure and reopening recommendations match observed behavior.

why: Adds business acceptance after test coordination and evidence capture are established. Business representatives remain the acceptance owners.
prerequisites: Required: agreed business scenarios, ready UAT environment/data, user access, participants and an acceptance decision process.
milestone: Facilitate one business scenario with a representative. Capture actual feedback and issues, and leave acceptance pending until their decision.

why: Begins design support with an evidence-based option review before larger architecture or code changes are proposed.
prerequisites: Required: requirements, quality targets, current technology landscape, team capabilities and delivery constraints.
milestone: Review two feasible options for one change. Confirm assumptions, cost/schedule constraints and unresolved technical risks are visible.

why: Uses a feasible problem scope and known quality needs to propose system boundaries that architects can review.
prerequisites: Required: reviewed requirements, feasibility evidence, existing architecture and platform constraints.
milestone: Walk one architecture proposal with a technical owner. Trace key requirements to components and record a meaningful tradeoff.

why: Makes APIs, data and integration behavior precise before implementation, building on known architecture boundaries.
prerequisites: Required: reviewed architecture, external contracts, data ownership rules and security/performance constraints.
milestone: Review one API and its data model. Confirm request/response examples, validation, error handling and compatibility rules are testable.

why: Adds user-facing design within the established product scope. It may run earlier in a UI-led project when research is already available.
prerequisites: Required: user goals and research, key scenarios, acceptance criteria, design system and accessibility needs.
milestone: Review a prototype journey with a user or product representative. Include success, error and recovery states plus accessibility checks.

why: Consolidates architecture, component and user-experience findings before code generation expands the change surface.
prerequisites: Required: relevant design artifacts, requirements, threat scenarios, security standards and accountable design reviewers.
milestone: Review a design containing a known security or testability gap. Confirm the gap is identified with an actionable mitigation and owner.

why: Introduces code changes after requirements, design and validation expectations can be supplied and reviewed with confidence.
prerequisites: Required: scoped work item, acceptance criteria, reviewed design, source code and an isolated development setup.
milestone: Implement one small feature with unit tests. A developer reviews the diff and verifies acceptance behavior in the isolated setup.

why: Checks feature code with deterministic unit and static checks. It can also be piloted earlier using existing developer-written code.
prerequisites: Required: source revision, runnable unit tests, installed dependencies, static-check configuration and agreed thresholds.
milestone: Validate a clean revision and a revision with a known unit-test or static-check failure. Confirm diagnostics identify the correct cause.

why: Adds review assistance once concrete diffs and validation evidence exist, making suggested findings easier for a reviewer to assess.
prerequisites: Required: code diff, linked requirement or defect, validation evidence, review standards and developer feedback.
milestone: Review a small change with a seeded correctness defect. Confirm the finding is actionable and resolved comments remain traceable.

why: Applies coding and review support to reproducible defects after triage, retesting and regression protection are available as practices.
prerequisites: Required: triaged defect, reproducible failure, affected code, expected behavior and runnable validation checks.
milestone: Fix one reproduced defect. Show the new protection fails before the fix and passes afterward, then obtain code review.

why: Introduces repository writes after code validation and review are established. Approval evidence is a real prerequisite to integration.
prerequisites: Required: approved change, required checks for that revision, merge policy, branch state and repository write authorization.
milestone: Merge an approved pilot change in an isolated repository. Confirm missing approval blocks integration and the resulting revision is recorded.

why: Creates traceable packages from integrated code so later pipeline and deployment steps can identify exactly what they handle.
prerequisites: Required: integrated source revision, version identifier, build scripts, dependency locks, toolchain and packaging rules.
milestone: Build a pilot revision twice. Confirm artifact identity, dependency manifest and provenance, and investigate any unexplained differences.

why: Adds an explicit policy check over pipeline evidence before deployment is delegated to a skill.
prerequisites: Required: pipeline run and revision identity, required-check policy, job results and produced artifact references.
milestone: Assess a run with a failed or missing required job. Confirm it cannot appear compliant merely because other jobs passed.

why: Automates repeatable test deployment after build identity and CI checks are established. Earlier test pilots can use manually deployed builds.
prerequisites: Required: validated artifact or corrected revision, working build/deploy pipeline, authorized test environment, configuration and rollback procedure.
milestone: Deploy a pilot build and then a corrected rebuild to test. Confirm versions and configuration, and demonstrate the recovery procedure.

why: Combines mature quality and delivery evidence into a release assessment. It recommends a position for human reviewers.
prerequisites: Required: release criteria, candidate identity, reconciled test/UAT evidence, security findings and operational readiness checks.
milestone: Assess a candidate with one unresolved release blocker. Confirm the blocker and evidence gap are explicit in the recommendation.

why: Turns readiness findings into an actionable deployment and recovery plan before any production execution is considered.
prerequisites: Required: candidate artifacts, production topology, dependencies, readiness findings, owners, change window and recovery requirements.
milestone: Rehearse one release runbook in a representative environment. Verify deployment checkpoints, rollback triggers and recovery validation.

why: Packages readiness and runbook evidence for the named human approver. It never substitutes its recommendation for approval.
prerequisites: Required: readiness assessment, test summary, deployment/rollback plan, exception requests and named human approvers.
milestone: Prepare a decision brief and verify every claim against evidence. Keep approval pending until the approver supplies a decision and conditions.

why: Handles rejected or conditional decisions before production deployment, keeping remediation ownership and reassessment evidence traceable.
prerequisites: Required: human decision, explicit blockers or conditions, remediation owners, corrective work and verification evidence.
milestone: Resolve one pilot blocker and update the evidence package. Confirm the release returns for reassessment instead of being automatically approved.

why: Comes late because production changes require dependable artifacts, approval, a rehearsed runbook and operational readiness.
prerequisites: Required: recorded human release approval, validated candidate, approved runbook/rollback assets, production access and monitoring/support readiness.
milestone: First pass a deployment and rollback rehearsal. Then, only with human authorization, complete a limited live release and record every checkpoint.

why: Adds AI support to established operational monitoring after controlled delivery. Existing monitoring and support must already cover any earlier release.
prerequisites: Required: telemetry, service targets, current deployment context, support tickets, runbooks, escalation rules and action authorization.
milestone: Replay a known incident. Confirm the assessment cites correct telemetry, follows escalation rules and performs only authorized runbook actions.

why: Closes the improvement loop once feedback and operational evidence can be interpreted. It can move earlier when suitable evidence already exists.
prerequisites: Required: user feedback, support cases, usage evidence, success measures, product strategy and the current backlog.
milestone: Review themes from one feedback period. Trace each proposed improvement to evidence and distinguish observed problems from assumptions.
